# Trellis AI guidance for Rust services

Last verified against Trellis main (2026-08-28).

Use this file for AI coding agents working in a Rust service repository that
consumes Trellis. The language-neutral guide is:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qlever-llc/trellis/main/docs/static/llms-full.txt

## Repository setup

- Expose contract/artifact generation through `cargo xtask prepare`.
- Commit the generated SDKs, participant facades, manifests, and package outputs
  expected by the repository. Never edit generated files by hand.
- Public contract object schemas are open by default. Omit
  `additionalProperties`; use `false` only for a documented proof/security
  boundary that must reject unknown fields.
- Run prepare after contract/schema changes. Generated owner and participant
  Cargo crates are materialized source with relative local dependencies and no
  generator `build.rs`.

## Rust architecture

- Connect only through the generated participant facade's `connect(...)`.
- Owner SDK crates contain typed vocabulary and thin adapters. They do not expose
  connection bootstrap, `ConnectedService`, or generic runtime clients.
- Service participants expose service bootstrap only. Apps and agents expose
  user-session bootstrap only. Devices expose activated-device bootstrap only.
- HTTP is limited to browser/account flows, initial service/device bootstrap,
  proof-bound restart recovery, and portal assets. Connected control,
  including auth control, uses generated RPC, operation, and event APIs over
  NATS; there is no HTTP context, revocation, logout, or client-bootstrap API.
  Pending devices retry `/bootstrap/device`; there is no separate wait or
  connect-info endpoint. Use `DeviceActivationOptions`,
  `check_device_activation`, and `wait_for_device_activation`, then hand the
  returned ready session into the separate pure `connect_device` entry point.
  Pending activation retains `server_now` and `expires_at` and derives a
  monotonic deadline from their difference. A changed review id is an explicit
  expired/replaced review. `Auth.DeviceUserAuthorities.Resolve` cancellation is
  unsupported.
- The participant facade embeds its canonical API and participant artifacts and
  their exact digests.
- Rust authoring supplies participant identity, API identity, and API release
  version independently. `ContractBuilder::authoring(participant_id, api_id,
  api_version, ...)` takes those values in that order;
  `ContractBuilder::from_api(participant_id, api, kind)` receives the version in
  the API artifact. `ApiBuilder::authoring(id, version, ...)` requires an explicit
  Semantic Version. Release version does not affect the semantic API digest.
  Generated participant facades expose `CONTRACT_ID`; generated API SDKs expose
  `API_ID`.
- Service connect options carry the immutable provisioned identity binding.
  User/device connect options carry the session-bound bootstrap JWT, session id,
  inbox prefix, session seed, and participant digest. No shared sentinel
  credential is configured or accepted. Ready bootstrap also carries a signed
  authorization-context bundle. The shared Rust cache verifies the root,
  direct-key manifest, signature, policy, and context digest, computes the
  deterministic refresh time, and supplies the current
  digest to every reconnect. Production user/service/device options require a
  durable authorization-context store containing the complete root/manifest
  rollback floor and current context; memory stores are explicit for tests and
  ephemeral processes. Clearing context retains trust. Bootstrap/refresh server
  time is converted to a request-midpoint offset. Expired context or route-JWT
  state recovers with a retained session/trust floor and proof-bound null current
  digest; same-digest success still reschedules. Context refresh is restart
  recovery and returns route/session/NATS metadata with the renewed route
  credential and context. Manifest overlap uses direct issuer public-key entries
  in the exact accepted generation. An observed `manifest.current` advance is
  persisted before the live floor advances and wakes the existing own-context
  refresh task. Connected trust lookup uses exact NATS KV direct reads and fixed
  manifest/revocation watches, not HTTP or whole-bucket access.
- The deny-all bootstrap JWT grants no authority. Context refresh is restart
  recovery: it renews the route credential and installs its exact expiry
  atomically with the verified context. It only routes Auth Callout and remains
  bounded by current session, authority, delegation, context, and the configured
  JWT lifetime cap.
- Runtime connection presence is retained for the resolved maximum user-JWT
  lifetime plus a 60-second cleanup grace, then exact records are removed after
  successful or already-absent physical connection kicks.
- Generated service/device clients present their embedded canonical participant
  and exact referenced API artifacts during bootstrap. Runtime planning parses
  and resolves them through the same semantic proposal path as admin planning.
- Dependency aliases become generated accessors. Absent aliases and unselected
  surfaces do not exist at compile time.
- Register owned RPC, feed, and operation providers through
  `service.handle()`. Used remote surfaces never appear under `handle()`.
- Use generated resource, state, Jobs, event-consumer, and publisher handles.
- Rust app and device facades expose declared value/map State stores. State is
  schema-validated by the Rust Platform owner, supports revision CAS and per-entry
  TTL, and follows the stable principal plus contract lineage. Services use KV
  resources instead; never open the internal `trellis_state` bucket.
- Do not import `trellis_rs::client` or `trellis_rs::generated` from application
  code. Do not extract NATS, credentials, bindings, subjects, or generic
  request/publish/subscribe methods.
- If a facade lacks a declared capability, fix the contract or generator. Do not
  add a transport shim in the service repository.
- Protocol tooling can call `trellis_protocol::resolve_participant(...)` with
  one validated participant artifact and its exact digest-pinned API artifacts.
  The pure result separates required and optional grant sets, provided APIs,
  private resource needs, capability/consent evidence, uncovered permissions,
  an alias-independent needs digest, and an authority-change fingerprint.
- Exact action selections remain authoritative. Capability evidence explains a
  complete selected permission bundle, identifies the exact defining API digest,
  and never expands the derived grant set.
- Resource bindings are physical evidence only; transport and request validation
  require exact `GrantSet` atoms. Missing optional evidence removes only the
  optional atoms it supports.
- Bootstrap replay resolves current issuance and signs a fresh credential.
  Externally serialized errors use stable redacted codes; internal causes belong
  only in structured logs.
- Pure protocol/tooling code can use `trellis-protocol` signed authorization
  types to verify a pinned root, root-signed direct-key issuer manifest,
  issuer-signed short-lived context, and
  context-bound request proof v1 without NATS, storage, wall-clock, or async
  access. Supply verification time and limits explicitly.
- Signed contexts bind principal and participant identity separately, exact
  participant/needs digests, authority version, session key, inbox prefix, exact
  grant set, and platform capabilities. Local checks compute the raw payload hash
  and enforce exact permission/capability subsets; capabilities never expand the
  grant set.
- Signed protocol integers, including nested extension integers and request
  `iat`, must remain within `-(2^53 - 1)..=(2^53 - 1)`. Context verification
  rechecks the current minimum manifest generation even for an already verified
  or cloned manifest handle.
- `maximum_context_bytes` is the canonical complete signed-context JSON UTF-8
  byte limit, not the base64url token length.
- NATS admission validates the signed context, NKey/session-key binding, and
  current physical bindings. Target
  providers then verify request/event proof v1 locally against the presented
  context, actual transport fields, exact generated permission atom,
  capabilities and revocation state. Provider
  authorization evidence comes from the internal NATS KV registry: watches for
  manifest generation and revocations establish readiness; actual connection or
  watch failure fails closed, while quiet watches remain healthy. Unknown
  current digests require one context read; cache hits perform no HTTP,
  SQLite, Auth RPC, or registry I/O. Registry handles and subjects are not
  service-author APIs.
- Event subject, Jobs key, and operation-transfer pointers must be guaranteed to
  resolve for every schema-valid payload. Every object step must be required and
  every array index must be covered by `minItems`; optional fields are invalid
  extraction paths even when their schemas have the expected type.

## Connection and authority

- `ServiceConnectOptions::new(trellis_url, name, deployment_id,
  provisioned_identity_seed_base64url, session_key_seed_base64url,
  authorization_context_store)` accepts runtime and credential inputs only.
  Generated `GeneratedServiceContract` constants are the sole source of service
  and device facade participant, API, digest, needs-digest, and referenced-API
  evidence; callers provide only runtime and credential inputs.
- Generated Rust device connection options do not accept a session key seed.
  Every activation/bootstrap attempt generates a fresh Ed25519 session key;
  pending attempts discard it, and only ready evidence carries the successful
  private seed into the exact connection handoff.
- Rust service bootstrap waits for pending deployment authority indefinitely by
  default. Use `ServiceConnectOptions::with_authority_pending_timeout_ms(...)`
  only when startup needs an overall deadline; `with_timeout_ms(...)` bounds each
  request.
- Bootstrap and admin planning share one semantic proposal path. Additive
  compatible changes are updates, incompatible API changes are migrations, and
  both require an authority decision. Deployment authority has one stable
  lineage per deployment + participant. Equivalent pending semantics reuse one
  proposal; terminal history remains queryable and never blocks reproposal.
- Only `pending` plans for the current desired authority version are actionable;
  older plans become `superseded`. Initial plans are listable before desired
  authority exists.
- Deployment authority acceptance commits desired state and returns while
  physical reconciliation continues in the background.
- Deployment authority `needs` group contracts, surfaces, capabilities, and
  resources. Materialized grants group capabilities, surfaces, and NATS rules.
- Trusted browser authority policy is keyed by exact portal + participant.
  Capability groups are recursive administrative macros, verified OIDC roles
  select provider-scoped mappings, and both are bounded by the participant
  proposal. Successful trusted local registration applies the same policy as
  local or OIDC login. Reconciliation revokes superseded contexts and exact
  matching connections. Removing a portal, provider allowance, or policy clears
  verified-role provenance, so restoring configuration requires a fresh verified
  login before authority returns. Sessions remain available for credential refresh.

## Typed calls

Call through the local participant alias:

```rust
let order = connected
    .client()
    .orders()
    .orders_get(&orders_sdk::OrdersGetRequest {
        order_id: "ord_123".into(),
    })
    .await?;
```

Match generated declared RPC and operation error variants directly. Do not
decode typed responses or errors back through JSON.

Start operations through generated invokers:

```rust
let operation = connected
    .client()
    .orders()
    .orders_process()
    .start(&orders_sdk::OrdersProcessInput {
        order_id: "ord_123".into(),
    })
    .await?;

let terminal = operation.wait().await?;
```

Operations are caller-visible workflows; Jobs are service-private execution.
Both remain bounded by transport permissions compiled from the connected
principal's current authorization context; declarations and subject strings
never create grants.
An operation or queue may declare one typed live update schema. Updates are
at-most-once, not persisted or replayed, and may be missed by late subscribers.
Prefer cumulative updates and treat terminal output/result as authoritative.

## Events

- Publish owned events through `service.publisher()` and generated
  `publish_<event>(...)` methods.
- Event subject params must resolve to string, number, or bounded safe-integer
  fields in every `anyOf`/`oneOf` branch. The runtime derives and escapes subject
  tokens from the payload; application code never builds subjects.
- Durable event processing is a declared `eventConsumers` resource. Register
  generated group handlers through `service.event_consumers()`.
- Trellis resolves durable names, filters, replay, and permissions from bootstrap
  bindings. Do not create JetStream consumers or inspect `num_waiting` as a
  readiness gate.
- Returned listener handles support abort/re-registration while retaining the
  Trellis-provisioned durable.
- Event handlers receive verified publisher metadata when proof validation
  succeeds. Event Log may validate retained historical session windows after an
  ordinary publisher context expires, but explicit context revocation
  invalidates every event proof from that context, including proofs created
  before revocation.

## Prepared events and inboxes

Direct typed publish is the default. Use a prepared event plus an outbox only
when event enqueue must commit atomically with service-local durable state:

```rust
use trellis_rs::service::{dispatch_outbox_once, OutboxStore, SqliteOutboxStore};

let publisher = service.publisher();
let prepared = publisher.prepare_orders_shipped(
    &orders_sdk::OrdersShippedEvent {
        order_id: "ord_123".into(),
        shipped_at: now_iso(),
    },
)?;

let tx = sqlite.transaction()?;
mark_order_shipped(&tx, "ord_123")?;
SqliteOutboxStore::new(&tx)
    .enqueue("outbox:ord_123:shipped", &prepared)
    .await?;
tx.commit()?;

let mut outbox = SqliteOutboxStore::new(&sqlite);
dispatch_outbox_once(&mut outbox, |event| {
    let publisher = publisher.clone();
    async move { publisher.publish_prepared(&event).await }
})
.await?;
```

Prepared events store subject, encoded payload, event id, and event time, but no
contract/deployment identity. Publish-time proof uses the current service
session. Use an inbox only when replaying a handler would not be naturally
idempotent.

## Jobs

- Low-level lifecycle event constructors live under `trellis_rs::jobs::events`.
  Build their shared service, job type, job id, context, and timestamp fields
  with `events::EventMeta`. Constructors for current-attempt events take `tries`
  separately; constructors for zero-attempt events do not. Constructors are not
  re-exported from `trellis_rs::jobs`.
- Clone submission queues through `service.jobs_client()` for RPC handlers,
  operations, and background tasks.
- Register workers through `service.jobs().<queue>().handle(...)` before
  `service.run()`.
- `service.run()` supervises workers and the authenticated request host. Any
  worker task exit fails the service.
- `JobRef` provides typed get, wait, and cancel behavior backed by lifecycle
  events.
- Retryable failures NAK before the final allowed delivery. The final retryable
  delivery remains unacknowledged so `AckWait` drives the durable MaxDeliver
  advisory; attempt and redelivery metadata come from JetStream. Keyed active
  slots are released best-effort before redelivery.
- Use `job.heartbeat()` for long processing, `job.progress(...)` for durable
  lifecycle progress, and `job.is_cancelled()` for cooperative cancellation.
- Keyed queues default to `fail-stale` and `reject`; coalescing/replacement must
  be explicit.
- Jobs admin uses `Jobs.Query`, `Jobs.Metrics`, `Jobs.Inspect`, and invalidation
  `Jobs.Watch`. `Jobs.List` and `Jobs.Get` are removed.

## Resources and transfers

- Access KV, store, state, and Jobs through generated named handles. They already
  contain resolved bootstrap bindings.
- Services use only the resolved handles returned by the connected facade; they
  do not fetch binding payloads or construct resource clients.
- Stream large store values with `StoreResourceHandle::write_from(...)` and
  `read_into(...)`; `write(...)` and `read(...)` are whole-buffer conveniences.
  The streaming write enforces the bound per-object maximum and an optional exact
  size while reading. Caller-owned writers are not flushed or shut down.
- Start transfer-capable operations with the generated builder's
  `.transfer_from(reader, expected_size).start()` when the body is not already in
  memory. Download grants support `download_transfer_into(...)`; the bytes helpers
  remain conveniences. Generated dependency aliases expose the same writer-based
  download methods. Transfer grants restrict frames to 1 byte through 1 MiB;
  cancellation is authenticated and acknowledged, and completion requires
  independent final size and SHA-256 verification.
- Providers receive `RequestContext`; capture
  `service.generated_handle()` at registration for resolved stores and other
  bound runtime resources.

## Testing and verification

- Test runtime-observable behavior with live integration tests. Do not use fake
  NATS, fake Trellis runtimes, fake auth, or fake generated clients.
- Shared-host integration cases use one NATS account, Trellis process, and SQLite
  set with one worker. Keep authored contract ids, actions, subjects, and
  participant identities fixed; case-scope only physical deployments, resources,
  durable names, state keys, and domain records.
- In the Trellis repository, the complete TypeScript and Rust live matrices run
  against one host with `deno run -A -c ts/deno.json integration/live_runner.ts`.
  The harness runs NATS as a managed child process from pinned, checksum-verified
  nats-server and nsc binaries (cached under `TRELLIS_TEST_CACHE_DIR`, default
  `~/.cache/trellis-test`; first use downloads them, requiring network; every reuse revalidates the cached archive sha256 against the pin and byte-checks the cached binary against a fresh extraction, so corrupted or replaced cache entries are reinstalled, and and `sh`
  must be on `PATH`); no container runtime is required.
- The `trellis` CLI runs the runtime with
  `trellis server [mode] --config PATH [--nats URL | --nats-binary PATH]
  [--nats-state-dir PATH] [--check]` (mode defaults to `all`; `--check`
  validates configuration, trust, stores, streams, and NATS connectivity,
  then exits). Managed mode (no `--nats`) downloads the pinned nats-server
  release, verifies its checksum, caches it under `TRELLIS_CACHE_DIR`
  (default `~/.cache/trellis`), listens on 127.0.0.1 ports 4222 (NATS), 8222
  (monitoring), and 8080 (websocket), and stops the server when the CLI
  exits. `--nats URL` runs against an external server; `--nats-binary PATH`
  manages an existing trusted nats-server binary without re-verifying it;
  `--nats-state-dir PATH` keeps all mutable managed-NATS files (rendered
  configs, pid file, resolver JWTs, JetStream data) outside a read-only
  bundle.
- The runtime OCI image bakes the `trellis` CLI and the pinned,
  checksum-verified nats-server at `/usr/local/bin/nats-server`; `nsc` is
  test-harness-only and not in the image. The entrypoint stays
  `trellis-server` for external-NATS deployments. For a managed single
  container, mount the generated bundle read-only from its own named volume
  and the writable state on a second volume
  (`trellis-bundle:/etc/trellis:ro,Z`, `trellis-state:/var/lib/trellis:rw,Z`),
  with the bundle's SQLite store paths rewritten to the state volume, and run
  `trellis server ... --nats-binary /usr/local/bin/nats-server
  --nats-state-dir /var/lib/trellis/nats`.
- Register client interoperability in `integration/client-test-matrix.json` and
  Rust runtime correctness in `integration/rust-runtime-test-matrix.json`.
  Implemented Rust mappings must match compiled and executed test IDs exactly;
  hidden skips are forbidden.
- Format changed Rust files and use focused checks in the inner loop. The release
  gate runs Clippy, curated pure tests, workspace Rustdoc with warnings denied,
  workspace doctests exactly once, and verifies lint-policy participation for
  every workspace crate. Trellis supports the current stable Rust toolchain; no
  older compiler compatibility is promised.
  Run `cargo xtask prepare` when generated artifacts change.
  Run `cargo xtask prepare --timings` to diagnose generation performance from
  phase and per-contract resolution times, subprocess counts, cache validation,
  generation outcomes, and installed file/byte totals. Prepare's persistent
  resolution cache is repository-namespaced, disposable, and stored in the user
  cache directory unless `TRELLIS_PREPARE_CACHE` overrides it. `--force`
  bypasses it. Contract resolution must be deterministic from tracked source;
  declare exceptional inputs under `[package.metadata.trellis.prepare]` with
  `inputs = ["relative/glob/**"]` and `env = ["VARIABLE_NAME"]`. Undeclared
  time, randomness, network, environment, and external-file inputs are
  unsupported.
